newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOLID BUYING SEES AUSTRALIA DLR THROUGH RESISTANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOLID BUYING SEES AUSTRALIA DLR THROUGH RESISTANCE.

text.p: The Australian dollar was spurred to break through US$0.7420 resistance by concerted buying from a Sydney-based U.S. player through morning trading, although sellers had appeared as the unit aproached US$0.7440.

The dollar also continued to strengthen on the cross rates, and showed little ill-effect from an overnight speech by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane that was interpreted as leaving rates with a bias to the downside.
By noon (0200 GMT) the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7429/34, up on an early US$0.7401/06 and Tuesday's local close of US$0.7391/96.
"It's basically been one buyer all morning. I reckon they've bought over 500 million this morning," said one trader, adding the buyer was an American institution in Sydney.

With the U.S. name leading the way, there had also been some investment bank buying as stop loss orders were triggered through the US$0.7420's, a level which had held the dollar in a rally during European trading overnight.
The dollar reached a morning high of US$0.7436 -- its highest level since August 1, when the unit was falling after a rally to US$0.75 had been rejected.
Resistance as the unit approached US$0.7450 was expected to cap the dollar on the day in the absence of fresh news.
"There's very good interest to sell up there. The market is still a little bit bid and will try to have another go at this level...and we'll get see what's up there."
Trade was mixed early as the market digested the contents of Macfarlane's speech in Perth on Tuesday night.
While Macfarlane was bullish on the growth outlook, saying growth above 4.5 percent was possible in the next few years, he said it was the inflation outlook that determined rate changes.
Given Australia's favourable inflation outlook, traders saw that as a sign that another easing was still a possibility.
The dollar has now put on almost one and a half cents since it hit two year lows of US$0.7295 on Friday, and the strength has not just been limited to gains against the U.S. dollar.
In trade weighted terms the dollar rose to 58.5 at noon, up from an opening 58.3 and a previous close of 58.1. The index has risen 0.9 points, or 1.6 percent, since Monday.
The dollar rose to 86.53/63 yen and 1.3841/54 marks from early levels of 86.12/22 yen and 1.3799/3812 marks and local closes of 85.81/91 and 1.3777/90. -- John Mair 61-2 9373 1800
